messages:
Maya (AE): Arcwell wants a 4-day POC next Wed. Requirements: Private/VPC connectivity, perimeter TLS inspection (their inline DPI rewrites SNI), and a single allowlist egress IP. Need a one-paragraph blurb for security, a pasteable fw snippet, and rough POC pricing. @Ibrahim @Zoe @Rita please.

Ibrahim (Solutions): Short: PrivateLink works but SNI-rewrite is risky for cert-based auth. Two practical patterns: (A) PrivateLink only: fastest, but if their DPI rewrites SNI or terminates TLS we may break mTLS/JWT validation. They would need a cert re-issue flow. (B) Connector/peering: deploy a small connector in their VPC or peer VPCs so DPI sees plaintext before traffic leaves. Connector preserves client IPs and audit logs.

Zoe (NetOps): Pasteable firewall snippet:
```
# Arcwell POC - Redwood allowlist (example)
# Replace <REDFW_EGRESS> and <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> with values we provide
ALLOW tcp from <app_subnets> to <PRIVLINK_ENI_CIDR> port 443
ALLOW tcp from <connector_subnets> to <REDFW_EGRESS> ports 443
ALLOW udp from <connector_subnets> to 8.8.8.8 port 53
# If using peering: allow ephemeral ports between VPCs
ALLOW tcp from <customer_vpc_cidr> to <connector_vpc_cidr> ports 1024-65535
```

Zoe (NetOps): We can allocate a single static /32 for the POC; production should use an HA pair. Note: PrivateLink ENIs are local IPs in their subnets; Redwood backend egress will still come from our managed IP(s).

Rita (Security): One-paragraph blurb for their packet: "Redwood will deploy an interface endpoint (PrivateLink) into Arcwell-managed subnets for the POC. Outbound model requests from the endpoint will egress from Redwood-managed static IP(s) provided for allowlisting. If Arcwells DPI rewrites SNI or terminates TLS, mutual-auth and cert-based validation may be affected; in this case Redwood recommends deploying a lightweight connector inside the VPC or peering with a connector VPC so inspection occurs prior to egress and audit logs and client IPs remain preserved."

Ibrahim (Solutions): Ballpark POC pricing to include in packet: static egress IP (POC, pro-rated) = $1,700/month per IP (estimate), connector VM = $500/month + $1,200 one-time setup, peering/config engineering fee = $1,800 one-time. Dedicated reserved capacity available for high throughput or many IPs (pricing on request). Numbers are illustrative until we issue a formal quote.

Maya (AE): Action items: Ibrahim to confirm IP(s) and send formal quote by EOD Tue, Zoe to attach a 1-page network sketch and minimum subnet sizing by Mon, Rita to drop the paragraph into their security packet. deploy-bot: New ticket POC-3367 created.

Ibrahim (Solutions): Acknowledged, will follow up with IPs and firm quote.

Zoe (NetOps): Acknowledged - will share topology Monday.

Maya (AE): Thanks team, will schedule kickoff with Arcwell.
